**Finding re-submitted: compliant** — no redline.

Nothing needed repairing on the substance; the verifier confirmed every element of the analysis and identified the sole failure as the deterministic `audit frequency limited` check, which cannot pass in a document containing no audit clause. I therefore kept the classification and made the rationale explicitly address why that check fails harmlessly.

Summary of the position:

- **No Vendor audit right exists.** Searches for *audit*, *records*, *inspect*, *verif* returned zero hits, confirmed by a full paragraph-by-paragraph read.
- **The two nearest candidates don't qualify.** §5 Fees and Payment (p0023) grants no examination or true-up right; §1 (p0001) obliges AP only to cooperate so Kubient can deliver the Services.
- **Outcome beats the preferred position.** With no audit right at all, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to cap.
- **Compliant, not missing.** Classifying this as "missing" would require inserting an audit obligation against our own client — the opposite of the rule's protective purpose.
- **Parked, not double-flagged.** Impressions being measured solely "as measured by Kubient" (p0009) with no AP-side verification right is a gap that runs *in our favour* to fix, so it belongs under the reporting/revenue-verification rule.
